record.original_question: Either find an abstract polytope P whose monodromy group Mon(P) is not a string C-group but which nevertheless has a unique minimal regular polytopal cover, or prove that no such polytope exists.

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Find a polytope P such that Mon(P) is not a string C-group, but P does have a unique minimal regular polytopal cover; or show the non-existence of such a polytope.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. An abstract polytope $P$ of rank $n$ is a poset (with a maximum and minimum element) satisfying the standard axioms: every flag has length $n+2$; $P$ is strongly flag-connected; and the diamond condition holds, i.e., for every $(i-1)$-face $F$ and every $(i+1)$-face $G$ with $F<G$, there are exactly two $i$-faces $H$ with $F<H<G$. For each $i\in\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ and each flag $\Phi$, there is a unique flag $\Phi^i$ that differs from $\Phi$ only in its $i$-face. The monodromy group $\mathrm{Mon}(P)$ is the subgroup of the symmetric group on the set of flags generated by the involutions $r_0,r_1,\dots,r_{n-1}$, where $r_i$ sends each flag $\Phi$ to $\Phi^i$. A string C-group of rank $n$ is a group generated by involutions $\rho_0,\dots,\rho_{n-1}$ satisfying the string property $(\rho_i\rho_j)^2=1$ whenever $|i-j|\ge 2$ together with the intersection condition $\langle \rho_i:i\in I\rangle\cap\langle\rho_i:i\in J\rangle=\langle\rho_i:i\in I\cap J\rangle$ for all $I,J\subseteq\{0,\dots,n-1\}$. An abstract polytope $R$ is regular if its automorphism group acts transitively on its flags; equivalently, regular polytopes correspond to string C-groups. A regular polytopal cover of $P$ is a regular abstract polytope $R$ together with a rank- and adjacency-preserving surjection $R\to P$. A minimal regular polytopal cover of $P$ is such a cover that does not factor nontrivially through another regular cover; $P$ has a unique minimal regular polytopal cover when (up to isomorphism) there is exactly one such minimal cover.

Problem. Either exhibit an abstract polytope $P$ such that $\mathrm{Mon}(P)$ is not a string C-group while $P$ nevertheless has a unique minimal regular polytopal cover, or prove that no such abstract polytope exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turn up the general framework (monodromy groups of polyhedra are automatically string C-groups, while in rank ≥ 4 minimal regular covers need not be unique, as illustrated by the Tomotope), but no published resolution of the specific question of whether a polytope with non–string-C-group monodromy can still admit a unique minimal regular cover. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Regular Covers and Monodromy Groups of Abstract Polytopes (Monson)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses when Mon(P) is a string C-group and the (non-)uniqueness of minimal regular covers; Tomotope as an example where Mon is not a string C-group.
status_evidence.claim: Background context indicates the question is nontrivial in rank ≥ 4 and no resolution is cited.

status_evidence.title: Minimal Covers of the Archimedean Tilings, Part II (Mixer)
status_evidence.snippet: Treats minimal regular covers of specific polytopes without resolving the general dichotomy.
status_evidence.claim: No general theorem given that closes the open question.
